title: Identity and Iowa origins
description: Marie Flodberg gives her name, nickname, age, and birthplace in Traer, Iowa, and identifies her parents as German immigrants. She recalls their migration through Illinois and Iowa and the family's move to Idaho by train with several other families.

title: Parents, farm life, and childhood deaths
description: She discusses her parents' backgrounds, her father's purchase of land and orchard work near Fruitland, and her mother's farm-household labor. She also recalls the deaths of her brother Rudolph and her grandfather and the home-funeral customs surrounding them.

title: Marriage, nursing, and abortion memories
description: She identifies her husband, Herman L. Flodberg, and describes her schooling, nursing training in Spokane, and early hospital jobs in Idaho. She also recounts assisting with abortions and meeting her husband while working as a nurse.

title: Work history and marriage circumstances
description: She explains the equivalence that let her enter nursing without a completed high school degree and lists jobs in Hailey, Pocatello, Moscow, Lewiston, and Orofino. She describes an independent married life shaped by work, money, and her husband's drinking.

title: Blindness, hobbies, and later life
description: She talks about losing her sight, her past gardening and prize-winning cooking and sewing, and her current routines in the Lewiston senior community. She also describes getting recorded magazines and books from the Library for the Blind.

title: Childhood memories, recreation, and advice
description: She recalls childhood pranks and Halloween mischief before turning to dancing, courtship, and why she married late. She resists giving younger women advice and ends by describing earning money sewing for neighbors as a girl.

title: Fabrics and nursing photos
description: Marie Flodberg talks about the cotton and silk fabrics she once used in dressmaking. Connie Richards then asks about old photographs, and Marie mentions she only has her nurses' pictures stored in a Kodak album somewhere.

title: Women's independence; sewing and Spokane buttons
description: Connie Richards asks Marie Flodberg how other women treated her for having a nontraditional career, and Marie explains she was independent and did not let it bother her. Marie then describes the sewing she did for friends, including a trip to the Crescent department store in Spokane to buy expensive buttons for a dress.

title: Secondhand dresses; aging and nursing shoes
description: Marie Flodberg explains how she acquired her current wardrobe from friends who had gained or lost weight. She discusses preferring long sleeves to hide blotches on her arms and confirms that she is wearing her old style of nursing shoes.
